I couldn't get his words out of my head

I feel the will to roam, to learn
By test, experience, nous,
That fire is hot and ocean deep,
And wolves carnivorous.

(rare) To replace something with something new
(rare) To replace a contract (especially a financial contract) with one or more new contracts.

novation.e: Borrowed from Latin novātiō (“a renewing, rennovation”), from novō, from novus (“new”). Compare novel, novelty.

s.d: (law) the replacement of one obligation by another by mutual agreement of both parties; usually the replacement of one of the original parties to a contract with the consent of the remaining party

(uncountable) Replacement of a contract with one or more new contracts, in particular in financial markets the replacement of a contract between a particular buyer and seller with contracts between the clearing house and each party.
x: A similar novation of infrastructure ownership was seen as a logical development for the operation of Merseyrail services. But this has remained with Network Rail, […].

novel.e: From Middle English novel, from Old French novel (“new, fresh, recent, recently made or done, strange, rare”) (modern nouvel, nouveau), from Latin novellus (“new, fresh, young, modern”), diminutive of novus (“new”). Doublet of nouveau.

s.d: an extended fictional work in prose; usually in the form of a story
a printed and bound book that is an extended work of fiction

he burned all the novels

s.d: A work of prose fiction, longer than a novella.
(historical) A fable; a short tale, especially one of many making up a larger work.
x: merry tales[…]such as the old woman told of Psyche in Apuleius, Boccace novels, and the rest, quarum auditione pueri delectantur, senes narratione, which some delight to hear, some to tell, all are well pleased with.

s.d: (obsolete) A novelty; something new.

Cognates

s.d: the momentary present
x: Now is a good time to do it
it worked up to right now

s.d: (uncountable) The present time.
x: Now is the right time.
There is no better time than now.

s.d: (uncountable) The state of not paying attention to the future or the past.
x: She is living in the now.

s.d: A particular instant in time, as perceived at that instant.
x: Forever is composed of Nows— / 'T is not a different time, / Except for infiniteness / And latitude of home.
Time is not thrust together and summed up out of nows, but the reverse: with reference to the now we can articulate the stretching out of time always only in specific ways.

nowhere.e:
